current_price_source: Yahoo Finance VNT.NZ regularMarketPrice, regularMarketTime 2026-09-18T04:08:13Z (NZX regular close; not an after-hours print). 52-week range NZ$5.65-8.40.

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted at 30-Jun-2026: 817,824,369 shares issued less 10,824,644 treasury shares (H1 FY2026 note 4.3) = 807.0m, plus 19.6m potential dilution from equity incentive plans (note 4.1 diluted-EPS adjustment) = 826.6m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. The on-market buyback (A$300m programme, A$185.8m used to 30-Jun-2026, continuing daily in H2 2026 at ~A$5.40-5.65) is value-neutral in this model and NOT netted from the count -- nor is its cash netted from net debt -- so both anchors are the same 30-Jun-2026 vintage.
inputs.total_debt_note: Gross borrowings A$1,050.0m at 30-Jun-2026 = A$750m syndicated facilities (two A$250m revolvers fully drawn + A$250m Asian term loan) + A$300m 6.283% AMTN notes due Jun-2033; carried at A$1,044.6m net of A$5.4m capitalised costs. A$400m revolver undrawn.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt = gross borrowings 1,050.0 - cash 480.8 = 569.2 (30-Jun-2026). Lease liabilities A$179.1m (47.6 current + 131.5 non-current) are EXCLUDED because the full lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B). Company-defined net debt incl. leases is A$748.3m. June cash is seasonally high and includes the A$300m note proceeds with revolvers still drawn.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 levered owner FCF, A$m: reported FCF 268.8 (OCF 378.9 - capex 110.1) - IFRS-16 lease principal 61.6 - SBC 5.9 = 201.3. Interest income (A$10.5m) NOT stripped: net borrower, cash is netted inside net_debt. The forward model is UNLEVERED (pre-interest) and component-built; FY0 unlevered owner FCF on the same components is ~A$264m (see last_fcf_unlevered_fy2025).
inputs.last_fcf_unlevered_basis: 6,141.1 x (8.66% underlying EBITDA - 0.10% SBC - 1.16% lease cash - 0.97% D&A ex-ROU) = EBIT 396 x (1 - 20.3% cash tax) + D&A 59.7 - capex 110.1 = ~A$264m (~A$226m at the 30% statutory rate). FY2025 cash tax (A$73.8m, 20.3% of underlying PBT) was below the 30% statutory rate; the model ramps 28% -> 30%.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: OCF 378.9 (post interest and tax, post lease interest) less capex 110.1 (PP&E 73.8 + intangibles 36.3); FY2025, statutory, includes A$2.5m TSRC novation proceeds.
inputs.sbc_source: VNT.NZ_Annual_FY2025.txt:7054 'Share-based payments 5.9 5.2' (operating cash flow reconciliation) and :7771 (statement of changes in equity). No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed; the A$28.0m 'payment for purchase of treasury shares' (FY2025 financing) is on-market share purchases to satisfy employee awards -- the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, so it is NOT added on top of the expense (that would charge the awards twice). Forward SBC set at 0.15% of revenue, above the 0.10% FY2025 actual, because the H1 FY2026 equity statement shows a A$16.6m gross reserve credit (A$7.5m net) -- the run-rate is stepping up.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received A$10.5m (FY2025) NOT stripped: net borrower (A$569m net bank debt), cash is not a surplus asset added to EV; it is netted in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 on-market buyback A$137.8m (29.1m shares at avg A$4.73) + A$28.0m treasury purchases; H1 FY2026 A$48.3m (8.6m shares at A$5.65). Programme raised to A$300m cumulative 2025-26; A$185.8m used by 30-Jun-2026. The flat count is FUNDED, not a convention.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-18T04:08:13Z NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime). Not an after-hours print. Bars for the last 5 sessions are populated (6.89 -> 7.49), so the quote is live, not frozen.
inputs.fx_rate_direction: NZD -> AUD multiplier (1 / AUD-NZD 1.2435): takes the NZX price to the AUD of the financials; used by scripts/sanity_check.py
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in AUD (Ventia files in Australia; 'A$' throughout the FY2025 annual report and H1 FY2026 4D); NZX quote in NZD. All per-share values computed in AUD then converted at AUD/NZD 1.2435 (Yahoo AUDNZD=X, 2026-09-19T04:50:56Z). Parity check on the ASX primary listing: VNT.AX A$6.00 (2026-09-18 close) x 1.2435 = NZ$7.46 vs observed VNT.NZ NZ$7.49 -- a 0.4% tie that confirms the rate, its direction and the quote basis. Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are NZD (quote currency); *_aud twins carry the model currency.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, single 8.5% rate across all three scenarios (owner-fcf.md s7f: risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario rates). Cost of equity: AU 10-yr government ~4.4% (Sep-2026, approximate) + 5.0% ERP x beta 0.9 (defensive contracted O&M book, 87% of FY26 revenue secured, but thin margins and a live cartel case) = 8.9%. Cost of debt: blend of BBSY+120-170bp bank facilities (~5.2%) and the 6.283% notes = ~5.6% pre-tax, 3.9% after 30% tax. Market weights E 90% (A$4.96bn = A$6.00 x 826.6m) / D 10% (A$569m net bank debt) -> 8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. The ACCC cartel litigation is charged in the BEAR flows and the 25% bear weight, NOT as a WACC premium.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US, contracted infrastructure services -> owner-fcf.md incl. section 7). Fresh build; no prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry for VNT.NZ. Component build on a 10-year horizon; FY0 = FY2025 actuals (31-Dec-2025), balance-sheet anchors 30-Jun-2026.

LEASES: treatment (B) -- leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal + interest) was A$71.0m in FY2025 (61.6 + 9.4 = 1.16% of revenue) and A$35.8m in H1 FY2026 (1.24%); charged in the flows via lease_cost_pct 1.2%. Lease liabilities A$179.1m are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A (1.0%) is ex-ROU: FY2025 depreciation 100.7 less ROU depreciation 61.6 = 39.1, plus amortisation 20.6 = 59.7 (0.97%).

EBITDA margin driver is the UNDERLYING post-IFRS-16 margin: FY2025 8.66% (A$532.1m; statutory A$557.0m includes the one-off A$24.9m TSRC novation gain), FY2024 8.2%, H1 FY2026 9.44% (record). Base Y1 9.5% back-solves to FY2026 underlying NPATA of ~A$279m (+8.3%), inside the 7-10% guidance; plateau 9.8% assumes only +0.3pp of further mix shift.

REVENUE: FY2026 base -1.5% (H1 -4.7% on the Defence Base Services transition; BST A$2.7bn from Feb-2026 and Clothing A$935m from May-2026 ramp into H2), then 5.0% -> 2.75% against an addressable market growing 4.7% CAGR (Oxford Economics, cited in the FY2025 annual report).

WORKING CAPITAL: net working capital is negative (contract liabilities A$388m + payables A$714m + employee/provision accruals exceed receivables A$435m + contract assets A$574m), so growth releases a little cash: +3% capture on the CHANGE in revenue (an outflow in the -1.5%/-4% revenue years).

CAPEX: FY2025 A$110.1m (1.79% of revenue, up from 1.13% FY2024 and 0.74-0.90% FY2022-23) on rig/well-services plant, SAP upgrade and new-contract mobilisation; H1 FY2026 A$61.0m gross. Base 1.7% -> 1.3% by Y5 (still above ex-ROU D&A of 1.0%).

TAX: cash tax rate ramps 28% -> 30% (statutory). FY2025 cash tax A$73.8m was 20.3% of underlying PBT (timing); the P&L rate was 29.9%; H1 FY2026 cash tax A$51.0m = 28.2% of PBT. PPA amortisation of acquired intangibles (A$4.0m FY2025) is inside D&A and immaterial.
UNLEVERED: interest paid on borrowings (A$48.8m FY2025, rising with the 6.283% notes) is not deducted from the flows because net bank debt is subtracted in the bridge.
NCI: none material (no non-controlling interests on the balance sheet); JV dividends (A$1.7m) stay in EBITDA.

ACCC CARTEL LITIGATION (civil, Federal Court, 30-day trial from 30-May-2027; alleged price-fixing of ADF estate-maintenance contracts 2019-22 with Spotless): charged in the bear scenario as a Y2 (FY2027) margin dip to 7.3% (~A$70m of penalty/legal/remediation) plus a permanent give-back to the FY2025 margin level (8.5%) and lower growth (Defence tender eligibility), and in the 25% bear weight. Not stacked into WACC (charge risk once).
CEO transition: Mark Ralston (12-year insider, ex-head of D&SI) commenced 1-Sep-2026; treated as continuity, no driver change.

Equity fell 630.9 -> 561.1 (FY2024 -> FY2025) despite A$272.2m profit because of A$137.8m buybacks + A$28.0m treasury purchases + A$178.4m dividends; this is capital return, not a data error, and equity CAGRs are therefore not used as the growth anchor.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward anchor: Oxford Economics addressable-market CAGR 4.7% (FY25-29) haircut for the FY2026 Defence transition year, cross-checked against revenue 3yr CAGR 5.9% and FY2026 guidance (NPATA +7-10% on flat-to-down revenue). Equity CAGRs are meaningless here (FY2020 equity A$33.7m was pre-IPO; FY2025 equity is being shrunk by buybacks) and EPS CAGRs are inflated by the FY2020-21 pre-IPO interest burden (A$137m FY2021 finance costs).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (75.5%) and EPS 5yr CAGR (47.2%) diverge from revenue 5yr CAGR (13.8%) by far more than 30pp: FY2020 is a pre-IPO base with A$33.7m equity and near-zero NPAT (A$28.0m) under the sponsor-era capital structure; the Nov-2021 IPO recapitalised the balance sheet (debt 1,313.9 -> 743.2). The 3yr figures (equity 2.5%, EPS 13.2%, revenue 5.9%) are the usable ones and equity is depressed by A$166m of FY2025 buybacks/treasury purchases. Neither CAGR family is used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - IFRS-16 lease principal - SBC, per year from the cash-flow statements. 3yr owner-FCF CAGR 3.9% vs reported 2.2%: lease principal was flat (A$59-64m/yr), so the gap is SBC noise, not lease creep. 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is not meaningful (FY2020 owner FCF A$0.4m after A$52.9m lease principal). FY2025 owner FCF fell 10% on FY2024 because capex rose A$41m (mobilisation/SAP) -- not an earnings decline (underlying EBITDA +6.6%). This series is LEVERED (post-interest); the forward model is unlevered.

scenario_narratives.base: Ventia converts its A$21bn work-in-hand and 87% FY26 revenue cover into a flat-to-slightly-down FY2026 (Defence Base Services transition) and then 4-5% growth as the A$2.7bn BST and A$935m Clothing Defence contracts, nbn Field Module/FTTN, Yarra Valley Water and the Victorian road contracts ramp -- broadly the 4.7% market CAGR. Underlying EBITDA margin lifts from 8.7% to 9.5% in FY2026 (guidance-consistent: NPATA ~A$279m, +8%) and plateaus at 9.8% as the mix keeps tilting to Energy/Water/Resources. Capex normalises from 1.8% to 1.3% of revenue after the rig and SAP programmes. The ACCC case settles or is decided without changing Defence eligibility. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 15x owner FCF (binds).
scenario_narratives.bull: New Defence contracts mobilise on time and Defence spending heads toward 2.3% of GDP, telecommunications wins (nbn, Optus) and the energy-transition/water pipeline push growth to 5-6.5% in FY2027-29, and the mix shift plus AI/digital productivity tools (VenSpark, VenSights) take the underlying margin to 10.6% by FY2031. Capex falls back to 1.2% of revenue and the buyback keeps the count flat at no cost to the model. ACCC outcome immaterial. Terminal growth 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Defence transition drags into FY2027 (revenue -4% then flat), the ACCC cartel case produces an adverse finding in mid-2027 with a penalty, legal and remediation cost of ~A$70m (FY2027 margin 7.3%) and a lasting hit to Defence tender competitiveness, insourcing and re-tender losses cap growth at 2-2.5%, and the margin settles back at the FY2025 level of 8.5% as labour inflation on fixed-price/unit-rate contracts erodes the mix gains. Capex stays at 1.5-1.8% of revenue to keep winning work. Terminal growth 2.0%. No solvency path: ND/EBITDA ~1.4x incl. leases, covenant 3.25x.

base.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF, A$m: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; x(1-cash tax); + D&A - capex + WC capture on revenue change. Pre-interest; net bank debt subtracted in the bridge.

bull.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF, A$m: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; x(1-cash tax); + D&A - capex + WC capture on revenue change. Pre-interest; net bank debt subtracted in the bridge.

bear.fcf_basis: Unlevered owner FCF, A$m: EBITDA - SBC - lease cash (principal+interest) - D&A ex-ROU = EBIT; x(1-cash tax); + D&A - capex + WC capture on revenue change. Pre-interest; net bank debt subtracted in the bridge.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the scenario's interim unlevered owner FCF (10 years) and exiting at year 10 returns a 15% IRR. Terminal value is rebuilt AT THE HURDLE: min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10). Net bank debt subtracted, divided by the flat diluted count, converted to NZD at 1.2435.
entry_price.note: A hurdle entry price near half of intrinsic value is the expected shape for a 3-5% grower discounted at 8.5%. The current NZ$7.49 implies a ~7.2% IRR on the base path (terminal value rebuilt at that rate; see required_return_table).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_10)). The 8.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario, NZD per share; rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. Terminal value = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10)) at each cell, so the cap flattens the right-hand columns at low WACC.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25% because the ACCC cartel trial (May-2027) is a dated, binary event touching the largest customer (Defence, 39% of revenue) that is itself mid-transition, and because thin ~9% margins give little room for execution error on A$3.6bn of newly mobilising contracts. Not higher: no solvency or covenant path (ND/EBITDA ~1.4x incl. leases vs 3.25x covenant), 87% of FY26 revenue secured, renewal rate 98.5%. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both a growth leg (5-6.5%) and a margin leg (10.6%) to come through in a business that has never printed above 9.5%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is ~0.15% of revenue, so house and street differ by only ~NZ$0.15/share; the band is near-degenerate (not null: SBC is small, not zero). A band position far outside 0-100% simply says the price sits well above both bases -- the SBC regime is irrelevant to the gap.

valuation_philosophy.basis: house: SBC fully expensed, lease cash charged in the flows, count held flat
valuation_philosophy.summary: Contracted O&M annuity with thin margins: value is a function of the margin plateau and the terminal multiple, not of growth. At NZ$7.49 (A$6.00) the market pays ~18x FY26 guided NPATA for a 4% grower.

methodology: Owner-FCF DCF, component-built, 10-year explicit horizon, end-of-year discounting, single AUD WACC 8.5%, TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10)), net bank debt bridge (leases in flows), flat diluted count 826.6m, AUD -> NZD at 1.2435.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
